review.assessment: The change increases `MAX_LEN` from 20 to 40 in `pubslug/slugs.py` to differentiate two specific article slugs by allowing a longer prefix before truncation. While this resolves the immediate collision between the August articles, it ignores the design constraint that a length of 20 is a hard limit for downstream catalogue columns and does not implement general collision resolution.

findings.actual: `MAX_LEN` is set to 40 in `pubslug/slugs.py`. This contradicts the docstring which defines 20 as a hard limit set by an external service for print catalogue columns. Changing it ignores this constraint and likely breaks downstream catalogue formatting.
findings.defect: Violation of External Constraints / Catalogue Width
findings.expected: `MAX_LEN` should remain 20, or collision resolution must be handled within that limit (e.g., via suffixes) to respect the external catalogue column width.

findings.actual: Slugs generated by `python run.py` may exceed the original report line shapes because URLs are now truncated at 40 characters instead of 20. The task explicitly forbids changing report line shapes.
findings.expected: Generated slugs and report lines must adhere to the original formatting constraints.

findings.actual: Slugs will still collide if two articles share a title prefix longer than 40 characters. The fix relies on input data properties rather than algorithmic uniqueness.
findings.at: Code logic in `pubslug/slugs.py` (truncation without collision fallback)
findings.expected: Slug generation should guarantee uniqueness for all inputs, typically through a suffix or increment mechanism when collisions occur.
